licenses.BlueOak-1.0.0: Permissive and OSI approved (Blue Oak Model License): use, change and redistribution with the notice kept, no copyleft. The isaacs packages (glob, minimatch, lru-cache, tar...) use it.
licenses.Python-2.0: Permissive and OSI approved (PSF licence): redistribution with the notice kept, no copyleft. argparse uses it.
licenses.Zlib: Permissive and OSI approved: redistribution with the notice kept, no copyleft. pako dual-states it with MIT.
licenses.CC0-1.0: A public-domain dedication with a permissive fallback: no condition on redistribution.
licenses.Unlicense: A public-domain dedication: no condition on redistribution.

packages.reason: libvips, shipped unmodified as a separate shared library that sharp loads at run time (Next.js image optimisation). LGPL allows distributing it with a non-LGPL program when it stays dynamically linked and replaceable by the user, and its licence and source location travel with the package. Only the web image contains it: in the backend tree it comes from a dev dependency (@react-email/ui).
Browser-support data, not code (browserslist via Next.js). CC-BY-4.0 asks only for attribution, which the package's own LICENSE carries.
pause@0.0.1 (passport) has no licence field; its Readme states the MIT License with its full text. Recheck if the version changes.
url-template@2.0.8 declares the non-SPDX id BSD; its LICENSE file is the BSD-3-Clause text.
